why.gap: EP-0006 established that r_safe is set by the number of concurrently running jobs competing for the pool, and measured it at concurrencies of 28.5, 54.2, 99.0 and 168.5 (r_safe 0.625, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5). Philly's 11cb48 -- the only real virtual cluster whose largest job is a large fraction of its pool (0.59) -- runs at a concurrency of 10.2, BELOW everything measured.
why.stake: Current Understanding v6 says that VC is on the safe side. That statement is currently an EXTRAPOLATION off the bottom of the measured range, not a measurement. This experiment turns it into one, or overturns it.

E9.design: hold the pool at N=256 (a realistic virtual-cluster size) and sweep concurrency by changing the background's granularity. Background = {s, 2s, 4s, 8s} with theta=0.4 weights; larger s means coarser background jobs and therefore fewer of them running at once.
E9.expected_concurrency: approximately 120, 60, 30, 15, 10, 7.5 (rho*N / E[k_background]); the actual value is measured, not assumed

detector: unchanged. r_safe = largest tested ratio at which the large class keeps flow balance >= 0.9.

predictions.claim: r_safe rises as concurrency falls below the range measured so far
predictions.criterion: r_safe at the cell whose measured concurrency is closest to 10 exceeds 0.625
predictions.falsified_if: it is 0.625 or lower, i.e. the curve is flat below 28.5 and the extrapolation in v6 was wrong

predictions.claim: r_safe is monotone non-increasing in concurrency across the whole sweep
predictions.criterion: ordering the six cells by measured concurrency, r_safe never rises as concurrency rises
predictions.falsified_if: any inversion larger than one grid step

predictions.claim: DECIDING. At Philly's actual operating point the margin is comfortable, not marginal: at the measured concurrency closest to 10.2, r_safe >= 0.75, so the VC's ratio of 0.59 has at least 0.16 of headroom
predictions.falsified_if: r_safe < 0.75, which would put Philly's 11cb48 within one grid step of the boundary and make v6's 'comfortably safe' reading wrong

predictions.claim: the sweep reproduces EP-0006 where they overlap: at the cell whose measured concurrency is closest to 28.5, r_safe is within one grid step of 0.625
predictions.falsified_if: it differs by more, which would indicate the two constructions are not measuring the same thing

predictions.claim: whole-pool jobs stay structurally starved regardless of how few competitors there are: at every s, m = N has flow balance < 0.5
predictions.criterion: flow balance(ratio=1.0) < 0.5 at all six s values
predictions.falsified_if: any s keeps the m=N class fed, which would mean even the structural case is a concurrency effect

predictions.claim: the harm at Philly's operating point is mild: at the cell nearest concurrency 10 and ratio 0.625, the large class's mean JCT is less than 5x the smallest background class's

pre_committed_consequence.if_W3_passes: v6's reading stands and is upgraded from extrapolation to measurement: Philly's riskiest virtual cluster has real headroom, and the domain's practical claim is that no examined production pool is near the boundary.
pre_committed_consequence.if_W3_fails: v6 is wrong on the real cluster's position. Philly's 11cb48 is near the boundary after all, the EP-0004/EP-0005 demotions get partially reversed, and the headline returns to naming a real production configuration as at-risk.

declared_unknowns: changing s changes the background's absolute job sizes as well as their count, so 'concurrency' and 'background job size' move together here; EP-0006 arm C already showed concurrency is the operative variable across a different construction, but this sweep alone does not re-separate them
N is fixed at 256 and rho at 0.85
